source_brief.title: PROJECT: APOPHYSIS REBORN — Complete Modernization of the Original Apophysis Fractal Flame Editor
source_brief.section_reference: Numbered sections 1–25 of the user-provided project brief; requirements below restate its named capabilities.

status_definitions.delivered: Working implementation with evidence for the stated bounded scope; target-platform acceptance is recorded separately.
status_definitions.partial: A useful subset exists, but a named part of the original requirement remains open.
status_definitions.missing: The requested capability is not implemented in this checkpoint.
status_definitions.platform_unverified: Code, binaries or verification instructions exist, but the relevant target-platform execution has not established acceptance.

counting_note: Rows group related requirements; counts are not a percentage of completion, a priority ranking or a complete catalog of every historical plugin.

requirements: Complete historical menu, control, parameter and variation inventory
requirements.scope_and_limit: Pinned source-level oracles, producer maps and a historical corpus exist. The complete cross-version inventory and every original application workflow are not audited; the supported subset must not be mistaken for full parity.

Tests compare the documented formulas, image reconstruction, palettes, affine operations and 7X curves with independent original-source fixtures. These bounded comparisons do not establish universal original-renderer equivalence.
All eight requested documents exist and link to precise implementation limits and evidence.
The distribution includes dependency notices, source provenance and corresponding source archives. Historical reference programs are separately generated; their scope and attribution are recorded.
Application, core, editor and tests are native code. Git history is restorable from the distributed bundle; normal editing/rendering needs no service login.

Windows binaries are cross-compiled and dependency-audited. Qt facilities and a Vulkan backend are present, but compilation and Linux/software-device execution do not establish target-platform acceptance.

Build/verification scripts and dependency instructions exist; M10 adds release tooling. Toolchains remain external development dependencies, and target-system setup still requires its documented prerequisites.
CUDA remains optional work; the implemented GPU API is Vulkan. Selecting an NVIDIA card does not select CUDA.
The admitted 2D model implements these operations with explicit producer conventions and validated transition weights. Symmetry generation uses explicit linear branches.

Supported scalar ranges, palette indexing, opacity and reconstruction rules are described per producer. Integer histogram accumulation and CPU double reconstruction are exercised by numerical and pixel tests.
Box and Gaussian reconstruction plus oversampling are implemented; other historical kernels and the complete original filtering surface remain open.
Active density estimation is rejected for rendering. Source fields remain preserved; no substitute operation is applied.

CPU seeds are reproducible across supported worker counts within the documented engine/build contract. Vulkan uses its own FP32 stream; historical RNG/x87 parity and universal CPU/GPU byte equivalence are not claimed.

requirements: All variations in the definitive original-source inventory
requirements.scope_and_limit: All 40 variations named in the brief are implemented. Noise, foci and pre_blur bring the registry to 43. Historical plugins and full producer-specific inventories extend beyond that list.

Implemented names accept signed finite weights; pre_blur has a defined pre-stage and supported explicit order is retained. Registered built-in parameters are editable; native modules register their own parameters. The claim applies only to implemented names.
The versioned 64-bit additive 2D CPU variation ABI supplies these controls. Data-only discovery does not execute modules; explicit approvals bind principal-library SHA-256 values.

requirements: Safe handling and isolation of native plugin failures
requirements.scope_and_limit: Descriptor, callback-error and nonfinite-result checks exist. Native callbacks still run in-process; access violations, crashes and hangs are not isolated by Lua limits.
A source migration example is included. Old 32-bit DLLs do not execute in this 64-bit application, and not every historical plugin API has an adapter.
The delivered ABI is a CPU variation API. Broader tool/automation extension hooks and user-plugin GPU kernels are not implemented.
The selected transform’s geometry and editable six-coefficient matrix stay synchronized. Completed drags are undoable; Esc restores a cancelled drag.
Current controls support admitted models; structural edits remap both Xaos axes and retain source identities. The parameter controls cover registered built-ins and enabled native modules.
Opacity and a temporary selected-transform canvas lock are present. Persistent per-transform lock/visibility state for a full multi-object editing workflow is not implemented.
The editor edits one selected transform; no general synchronization tool, custom increment profile or multi-selection geometry workflow is exposed.
The Reborn generator produces 1–24 candidates using explicit constraints, named seeds and useful-orbit framing. This is its own algorithm, not historical random-sequence parity.
Private candidate workflows, original-parent comparison and saved ancestry are implemented. Applying or adding a result is undoable; zero strength retains the parent parameters.
Reborn supports reproducible generation and saved linear ancestry. Historical generator output, a favorites manager and a general branching history-tree interface remain open.

A 256-entry gradient editor supports GPL/UGR/MAP and flame-palette exchange, local palette presets, palette curve baking, RGB/linear-light RGB/shortest-hue HSV/HSL interpolation and original/continuous reconstruction curves.
PNG/TIFF output supports straight RGBA8/16. Alpha is selected for output; the stored flame background remains RGB.
Embedded colors and personal GPL presets work. Missing historical catalog indices are not resolved, and a full palette-library folder/tag manager is not present.
Direct-color variation families are not implemented; weighted tone curves do not supply direct-color variation semantics.
The Adjustment and Render dialogs expose the documented supported controls; numeric changes preserve producer conventions and are privately previewed before Apply.
Palette saturation is edited in Gradient; transparency is an export option. These are not a complete recreation of all version-specific historical Adjustment fields.
The current renderer uses documented fixed numeric paths and a bounded control subset. These omitted controls are not silently replaced by similarly named modern values.
Current fields have validation and many tooltips, but full historical control coverage and a tooltip audit across every dialog are unfinished.
The current CPU and Vulkan implementations share the supported model and reconstruction contract. Runtime identity and fallback reason remain visible; the CPU path is always available.

requirements: Physical GPU performance and vendor-driver correctness
requirements.scope_and_limit: Software Vulkan checks exercise dispatch and numerical contracts, not NVIDIA/AMD/Intel hardware speed or Windows drivers.

Applicable pre-commit capability/allocation failures can fall back to CPU. Once GPU sampling commits, checkpoint identity prevents mixing CPU samples into that job; arbitrary driver failures cannot be promised recoverable.
Kernel workgroups/chains and bounded dispatch are implementation choices, not a general end-user GPU tuning panel.
M10 adds a repeatable host benchmark runner and machine-readable observations. A host report must be read with its binary/device identity; physical target-system measurements remain separate.

The renderer samples at the selected full dimensions and reconstructs bounded strips with filter overlap. The M7 full-size image and complete decoder/seam evidence remain historical acceptance records.
The preflight planner checks bounded working allocations, dimensions, output capabilities and conservative storage. The buffer budget is not a cap on whole-process or driver RSS.

Queue phase ETA uses observed progress; benchmark reports record actual timings. Preflight reports resources, not an invented pre-render finish time. There is no persistent machine-calibrated prediction model.
Integer output depth is selectable. CPU double math, Vulkan FP32 orbit math and integer hit accumulation are fixed backend contracts, not arbitrary user-selected histogram precision.
The preview controller discards stale results and cancels superseded work. Preview zoom changes display magnification; saved camera/output dimensions use their own controls.
The current preview is an opaque reconstruction of the flame background. Transparent export is available, but a checkerboard compositing preview is not exposed.
PNG/TIFF provide RGB/RGBA8/16; PPM provides RGB8/16; BMP provides RGB8. Streaming encoders reject unsupported alpha/depth combinations.
These are not image export formats of the renderer. A Qt image plugin or a 16-bit integer container does not add these capabilities.
Outputs are tone-mapped integer channels without invented ICC/HDR metadata. PNG compression and TIFF layout are fixed; complete flame parameters are saved separately.

Projects and canonical flames can be saved separately; queue/script/animation batches are supported. Animation uses a prefix and global frame number, not an arbitrary token-template language. Automatic image-sidecar/embedded metadata export is not implemented.
The document layer preserves original bytes and reports render blockers per selected entry. Parsing a file is distinct from rendering all of its historical settings.
UGR/MAP/GPL, the identified Apophysis UPR profile and a strict Pascal subset are supported. Arbitrary Ultra Fractal formulas/layers and complete historical script behavior remain unsupported.
Native project settings/presets are implemented; there is no general importer for the original applications’ settings files and full preference schemas.

Source-preserving save and supported canonical/UPR export have different fidelity. Original Windows editor reopening and complete renderer comparison remain unverified; modern curve/project markers are not historical compatibility guarantees.

The bounded versioned .apoproject envelope retains the exact collection and unknown envelope data. Projects do not authorize plugin loading; timelines cannot be silently lost through a plain-library Save.

Embedded Lua operates on a private source-preserving document; capabilities, inputs, output planning and resource limits are host-controlled. Apply and external publication have documented separate commit boundaries.
A tested Pascal subset rejects unsupported syntax/APIs during full preflight. User procedures, arrays/records, many original globals and original RNG output are not implemented.
The timeline and animation CLI exist, and script snapshots retain curves/time metadata. Dedicated Lua/Pascal APIs for timeline/keyframe editing and tone-curve controls are not supplied.

Version-1 Reborn clips use exact source snapshots, rational timing, stable correspondence, explicit interpolation/topology policies and bounded selected-frame export. Discrete values hold; unsupported continuous combinations are diagnosed.

Legacy time import requires explicit units and Reborn morphs use explicit IDs/pairing. Full historical interpreter parity, automatic matching, per-property tracks and subframe motion sampling are not implemented.
No video encoder, audio track or FFmpeg integration is bundled. Frame sequences can be processed separately.
Current Qt workflows provide these functions for the implemented subset. Dialogs are separate private-edit windows; not every creative window is a dockable workspace.
The shipped theme is dark; recovery is fixed at 45 seconds. Saved panel state and default reset do not provide a full workspace/profile system.
Document undo is bounded and functional, but a history-browser UI is absent. Native Windows DPI/multi-monitor/restore behavior needs target-system execution.

One background worker runs sequential jobs; phase ETA appears only after measured progress. Restored work stays stopped, saved jobs retain exact integer settings and plugin identities, and removal does not delete outputs/checkpoints.

Only committed immutable chunks resume. Identity, corruption, locks, partial publication and real process-interruption cases are covered. Checkpoints are not portable cross-build archives and reconstruction may restart from strip one.
The queue is deliberately sequential and does not invoke operating-system power management. Parallel CPU workers are per job, not simultaneous queue jobs.
Implemented preferences persist through Qt settings or native projects as documented; render-specific settings remain distinct from source flame parameters.
Many corresponding controls exist within individual tools, but the complete original preference dialogs, default ranges and replacements are not yet catalogued or recreated.
No language/profile/Sheep preferences are exposed. CLI checkpoint paths are explicit; native queue/cache paths use the application-local directory and the queue runs one job.
The admitted model and host requests are checked before commit; failed writes retain prior destinations. Source, queue and external files have explicit distinct transaction boundaries.

Host validation cannot isolate native crashes/hangs or promise recovery from arbitrary driver failure. Native code remains explicitly trusted and GPU checkpoint streams cannot silently switch backend after commit.
M10 system/build information helps diagnosis but is not automatic native minidump collection or a crash-reporting pipeline.
The editor has a rotating text Activity log and multiple JSON reports. M10 adds build/system diagnostics; there is no unified structured event/crash log covering every subsystem.

The native suites execute actual functions, rendering and Qt event workflows; full results and exact source scopes are recorded per release. Tests of unavailable features such as density estimation do not exist.

requirements: Windows runtime and physical-GPU test execution
requirements.scope_and_limit: Delivered target scripts and cross-compiled executables are not execution evidence. Real Windows 11 and supported physical devices still require their own reports.

The complete M7 acceptance and independent full-image decoder/queue/restart records establish the historical implementation result. They remain labeled M7; consult current release records for any separately rerun large case.
M10 records measurements on the actually available host; no target-system speedup or unmeasured hardware prediction is implied. Host benchmark reports and final hashes accompany the release.
Milestone source, tests and history are retained; the release handoff identifies exact continuation gates. Numbering does not waive remaining requested capabilities.

requirements: Complete requested product by milestone completion
requirements.scope_and_limit: 0.10.0 is a release-hardening checkpoint, not a claim of completed historical parity or 1.0 acceptance. The remaining-work list below remains part of the project scope.
The complete source distribution and runtime deliverables retain these materials; exact archive inventory and source identity are recorded by the release gate.

M10 supplies a versioned per-user installer with bounded payload/uninstall rules. Its actual target Windows lifecycle needs Windows execution; static payload checks or Wine do not establish that acceptance.
The application includes a fractal window icon and example/preview assets. A complete branded shell/icon-asset family is not part of the historical-parity claim.
Available-host measurements are recorded; Windows and physical-GPU benchmark reports remain unverified until run on those systems.

M10 centralizes 0.10.0 build metadata and exposes source/compiler/target information. Reproducible source/bundle identity is verified; universal byte-reproducible builds across toolchains are not claimed.

The application is native and offline, with a validated 16384-per-side renderer limit and explicit capability blockers. This does not satisfy missing historical features by substituting a simplified formula.
The explicit omissions in sections 3–9, 14–19 are still requirements. The existence of the native renderer and M10 package is not completion of the entire recreation brief.

requirements: Supply exact commands for unavailable Windows/hardware checks
requirements.scope_and_limit: The packaged validation and handoff distinguish available-host execution from pending target-system tests. No absent target run is represented as success.
